qualifying_findings.title: Visual Studio adds custom agents and branch-aware AI workflows
qualifying_findings.visible_date_basis: Article page and search result show an August 25, 2026 publication date.
qualifying_findings.short_factual_summary: Microsoft described Visual Studio agent-mode updates including bring-your-own model selection, custom agents for repository-specific workflows, generated pull-request descriptions, branch-linked chat and code context, code-review comment handling, and a choice between delegating work to GitHub Copilot coding agent or applying fixes locally.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: The practice signal is that IDE coding agents are becoming multi-model, branch-aware, and review-comment aware; local guidance should treat custom agents and branch context as durable workflow inputs that need ownership, verification, and review evidence.
qualifying_findings.local_practice_implication: Custom IDE agents should be tracked as maintained instruction surfaces with branch context, model routing, PR-description generation, and review-comment fix loops included in acceptance evidence.

qualifying_findings.title: JetBrains publishes modern Go skills for AI coding agents
qualifying_findings.visible_date_basis: URL path and search result show 2026/08/24 and August 24, 2026.
qualifying_findings.short_factual_summary: JetBrains published Modern Golang Skills, a repository of reusable AI skill files intended to guide agents toward current Go practices, including standard library evolution, error handling, concurrency, slog logging, SQL access, testing, fuzzing, benchmarking, generics, modern CLI development, and cloud-native patterns.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: This is a concrete durable-instruction pattern: language and framework practices are packaged as reusable skills so coding agents can load maintained guidance instead of relying on stale model priors.
qualifying_findings.local_practice_implication: Treat language-specific skill packs as governed reusable instruction artifacts with provenance, update cadence, scope notes, and verification expectations before adoption.

qualifying_findings.title: JetBrains introduces local execution for Junie
qualifying_findings.visible_date_basis: URL path and search result show 2026/08 and one-day-old publication within the cutoff window.
qualifying_findings.short_factual_summary: JetBrains announced Junie Local, describing a path for running its coding agent workflow in a local development environment rather than only through remote execution.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: Local execution changes the governance checklist for coding agents: workstation permissions, repository trust, local dependency installs, secrets exposure, filesystem access, and reproducible verification become first-class adoption questions.
qualifying_findings.local_practice_implication: Route product specifics upstream; locally capture the local-agent environment-readiness checklist and the delta between local and managed sandbox execution.

qualifying_findings.title: Decoding AI frames context engineering as system-state design
qualifying_findings.visible_date_basis: Article page and search result show August 24, 2026.
qualifying_findings.short_factual_summary: Decoding AI published a context-engineering overview that emphasizes assembling the right system state around the model, including instructions, retrieved knowledge, tools, memory, schemas, and workflow-specific data rather than treating prompting as the whole design surface.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: The local wiki already owns context routers, knowledge layers, and compaction; this source is useful as current corroboration that context architecture should be designed as a repeatable system boundary, not as ad hoc prompt text.
qualifying_findings.local_practice_implication: Ingest only the downstream practice angle: context packages should name state inputs, retrieval provenance, tool affordances, memory scope, and schema contracts for each coding-agent workflow.

qualifying_findings.title: Trust3 highlights OAuth and token-scoping controls for MCP
qualifying_findings.visible_date_basis: Article page and search result show August 24, 2026.
qualifying_findings.short_factual_summary: Trust3 published an MCP security guide focused on OAuth tokens, delegated access, and the expanded attack surface created when AI tools act across connected services.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: The useful local signal is not broad MCP background, which is upstream-owned, but the practice requirement that MCP access for coding agents needs scoped authorization, token handling rules, approval evidence, and auditability.
qualifying_findings.local_practice_implication: Use this as governed-MCP evidence for scoped tokens, connector identity, revocation, explicit approval packages, and log retention around tool calls.

qualifying_findings.title: Towards AI describes safeguards for AI-generated code review
qualifying_findings.visible_date_basis: Article page and search result show August 24, 2026.
qualifying_findings.short_factual_summary: Towards AI published a practice article on reviewing AI-generated code with safeguards around correctness, maintainability, tests, security, and disciplined review instead of accepting generated diffs at face value.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: This aligns with the local structural and layered review leaves: generated code requires source-backed review, risk-tiered checks, tests, and human acceptance criteria before merge.
qualifying_findings.local_practice_implication: Use as a current practitioner corroboration source for review rubrics that combine tests, static analysis, dependency review, maintainability checks, and human ownership.

qualifying_findings.title: Towards AI proposes application evaluation for LLM systems
qualifying_findings.visible_date_basis: Article page and search result show August 23, 2026, inside the two-day cutoff.
qualifying_findings.short_factual_summary: Towards AI published an evaluation-focused article that treats LLM quality as an application-level concern requiring task-representative checks rather than only model-level benchmarks.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: The local practice implication is that coding-agent and AI-assisted development evals should be workflow-specific, include tool and context behavior, and preserve examples that represent real repository work.
qualifying_findings.local_practice_implication: Route broad LLM-evaluation background upstream; locally capture representative workflow calibration, trace evidence, and acceptance-gate placement for software-delivery agents.

qualifying_findings.title: OpenAI community thread surfaces safe MCP setup confusion
qualifying_findings.visible_date_basis: Forum thread metadata in search result shows one-day-old activity inside the cutoff window.
qualifying_findings.short_factual_summary: An OpenAI community thread asked about safe MCP setup with ChatGPT and the practical security expectations around connecting tools.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: The item is low-authority but useful as adoption evidence: users need concrete setup guidance, connector-scope explanations, and visible approval or denial behavior when enabling MCP-like tool access.
qualifying_findings.local_practice_implication: Keep this as adoption-friction evidence for setup checklists and approval explanations; do not use it as authoritative security guidance.
